true_positives.golden_comment: The downsize method is defined twice. The second definition, which expects a single dimensions string parameter, overrides the first, which expected separate max_width and max_height parameters. This makes the original method unreachable and breaks existing code that calls it with separate width and height arguments.
true_positives.matched_candidate:
Duplicate `downsize` method overrides the 4-argument API

There are two definitions of `OptimizedImage.downsize` in this file (lines 145 and 149). In Ruby the second definition completely replaces the first, so the 4-argument `downsize(from, to, max_width, max_height, opts)` API no longer exists. Any existing caller passing two numeric dimensions will now invoke the new `downsize(from, to, dimensions, opts)` method: the third argument is treated as an ImageMagick geometry string and the fourth as an options hash, causing `TypeError` (`Numeric#[]`) or an invalid `-resize` command. The old method should be removed or renamed, and all callers updated.

true_positives.golden_comment: Hardcoding maxSizeKB = 10 * 1024 ignores Discourse.SiteSettings['max_' + type + '_size_kb'], so the client-side limit can diverge from server-side and per-type settings (also applies to the 413 handler below).
true_positives.matched_candidate:
Client-side upload size limit hard-coded to 10MB for all types

`maxSizeKB` is hard-coded to `10 * 1024` instead of reading `Discourse.SiteSettings['max_' + type + '_size_kb']`. This applies to both images and attachments. If the site has a lower `max_attachment_size_kb`, users can now upload attachments up to 10MB from the browser, and the server-side change in this PR does not downsize non-image attachments. This bypasses configured upload limits and may allow abuse or disk exhaustion.

false_negatives.golden_comment: Passing 80% as the dimensions can fail for animated GIFs when allow_animated_thumbnails is true, since the animated path uses gifsicle --resize-fit which expects WxH geometry, not a percentage; downsizing would then silently fail.
The loop checking `tempfile.size` may never terminate correctly due to stale cached size, leading to potential infinite loops or incorrect file handling after modifications.

false_positives.candidate:
413 error message shows hard-coded 10MB limit

The 413 error path now displays a hard-coded 10 MB limit regardless of the site's actual `max_image_size_kb` or `max_attachment_size_kb`, so the user may see an incorrect accepted size. Use the configured value or a generic message.

API URL download limit hard-coded to 10MB for all file types

The API URL upload path now downloads up to `10.megabytes` for every file type, instead of respecting `SiteSetting.max_image_size_kb` or an attachment size limit. The new downsize loop only applies to images, so a non-image URL up to 10MB is passed to `Upload.create_for` even when the site's max attachment size is lower. This bypasses the configured server-side upload limit.

Downsize failure is ignored and oversized images may still be saved

`OptimizedImage.downsize` returns `false` when ImageMagick/gifsicle fails (see `convert_with`), but this loop ignores the return value and simply retries. After five failed attempts it proceeds to `Upload.create_for` with the still-oversized file. If image processing is unavailable or repeatedly fails, an oversized image is stored, defeating the site's `max_image_size_kb` limit.

No tests added for automatic downsize behavior

No tests were added for the new automatic downsize behavior, particularly failure paths where `OptimizedImage.downsize` returns `false`, or for the duplicate `downsize` method in `OptimizedImage`. Without coverage, these regressions are likely to go unnoticed.

true_positives.golden_comment: The EmbeddableHost model's before_validation callback calls self.host.sub! to strip http://, https://, and path segments, but if self.host is nil, this raises NoMethodError.
true_positives.matched_candidate:
before_validation crashes when host is nil

The `before_validation` block calls `self.host.sub!` and `self.host.sub!` without checking if `host` is nil. If a host record is created or updated with a nil host (e.g., due to missing params), this will raise a `NoMethodError`. The controller always attempts to set `host.host` from `params[:embeddable_host][:host]`, but if that param is absent, the value remains nil. The model should handle nil gracefully, either by skipping the callback or adding a presence validation.

true_positives.golden_comment: The update and destroy methods in Admin::EmbeddableHostsController do not validate the existence of the EmbeddableHost record retrieved by ID. If EmbeddableHost.where(id: params[:id]).first returns nil (i.e., the host does not exist), attempting to call methods on the nil object (e.g., save_host or destroy) will result in a NoMethodError.
true_positives.matched_candidate:
Destroy action does not handle missing host record

Similar to update, `destroy` fetches `host = EmbeddableHost.where(id: params[:id]).first` without checking for nil. If the id does not exist, `host.destroy` raises a `NoMethodError`, causing a 500. The controller should return a 404 when the host is not found.

true_positives.golden_comment: Because this migration inserts embeddable_hosts rows with raw SQL, any existing embeddable_hosts values that include http:// or /https:// or path segments won’t go through the EmbeddableHost model’s normalization, so the new host lookup (which compares only the bare host) may fail for migrated data. Consider ensuring that migrated hosts are normalized to the same format as newly created EmbeddableHost records so existing embedding configurations keep working.
true_positives.matched_candidate:
SQL injection and missing normalization when migrating host values

The migration uses raw string interpolation to insert host values: `execute "INSERT INTO embeddable_hosts ... VALUES ('#{h}', ..."`. This is vulnerable to SQL injection if the old `embeddable_hosts` setting contained a quote. Additionally, the inserted hosts are not normalized (e.g., stripping `http://` or paths), unlike the model's `before_validation` which does so on save. As a result, migrated hosts will not match when `EmbeddableHost.record_for_host` compares `lower(host)` against the URI host, breaking embed functionality until each record is manually edited and saved. Parameterized queries and application of the same normalization logic should be used.

true_positives.golden_comment: The contents of `category_fabricator.rb` and `embeddable_host_fabricator.rb` have been swapped, resulting in the loss of original category fabricators and potentially causing errors in fabricator usage.
true_positives.matched_candidate:
Category and embeddable_host fabricators appear swapped between files

The file `spec/fabricators/category_fabricator.rb` now contains `Fabricator(:embeddable_host)` instead of category fabricators, while `spec/fabricators/embeddable_host_fabricator.rb` contains the original category fabricators. This is almost certainly an accidental swap during file creation. While it may still work because Fabrication loads all `.rb` files regardless of name, it is confusing and likely unintended. The category fabricators should be in their own file and the embeddable_host fabricator in its own.

true_positives.golden_comment: The SQL query in the `app/controllers/admin/embeddable_hosts_controller.rb` file uses string interpolation (`'#{h}'`) to insert values, which is vulnerable to SQL injection. It should use parameter binding or proper quoting to prevent this security vulnerability.
true_positives.matched_candidate:
SQL injection and missing normalization when migrating host values

The migration uses raw string interpolation to insert host values: `execute "INSERT INTO embeddable_hosts ... VALUES ('#{h}', ..."`. This is vulnerable to SQL injection if the old `embeddable_hosts` setting contained a quote. Additionally, the inserted hosts are not normalized (e.g., stripping `http://` or paths), unlike the model's `before_validation` which does so on save. As a result, migrated hosts will not match when `EmbeddableHost.record_for_host` compares `lower(host)` against the URI host, breaking embed functionality until each record is manually edited and saved. Parameterized queries and application of the same normalization logic should be used.

true_positives.golden_comment: The migration accesses execute(...)[0]['id'] without checking if the query returned any rows, which causes a crash when no embed_category setting exists. This can lead to a broken feature when attempting to edit category/host relationships.
true_positives.matched_candidate:
Migration fails if embed_category setting is missing or has no matching category

The migration executes `SELECT c.id FROM categories AS c INNER JOIN site_settings AS s ON s.value = c.name WHERE s.name = 'embed_category'` and immediately calls `[0]['id']`. If the `embed_category` site setting does not exist or its value does not match any category name, the query returns no rows, and `[0]` is nil, causing a `NoMethodError` and aborting the migration. This would break upgrades for any forum that has not configured `embed_category` or has it set to a non-existent category. The code should check for the existence of a result before accessing `[0]`.

false_negatives.golden_comment: record_for_host compares lower(host) = ? but does not normalize the parameter’s case, so mixed‑case referer hosts may fail to match even though comparison intends to be case‑insensitive.

false_positives.candidate:
Removal of embeddable_hosts check may expose expandable posts when no hosts configured

The `expandable_first_post?` method previously required `SiteSetting.embeddable_hosts.present?` in addition to `embed_truncate?` and `has_topic_embed?`. With the removal of that check, if `embed_truncate` is true and a topic has an embed (perhaps from old data), the expandable feature will be enabled even when no embeddable hosts are configured in the new table. This could lead to unexpected UI behavior for forums that have embed_truncate enabled but no allowed hosts.

Serializer produces embeddable_hosts as ids but client store expects embeddable_host_ids

The serializer uses `has_many :embeddable_hosts, embed: :ids`, which outputs a key `embeddable_hosts` containing an array of ids. However, the client store's `_hydrateEmbedded` method looks for keys ending in `_ids` (e.g., `embeddable_host_ids`) to hydrate plural associations. As a result, the embedding model will not have its `embeddable_hosts` property set to a collection of models; instead it will contain a plain array of ids. The template `embedding.hbs` iterates over `embedding.embeddable_hosts` and passes each item to the `embeddable-host` component, which expects a model, leading to runtime errors and an empty/broken admin page. The `embed: :ids` option should be removed so that the default rest serializer includes `embeddable_host_ids`, or the client code must be updated to handle the plural association name.

Update action is a no-op and may mislead the frontend

The `update` action in `Admin::EmbeddingController` simply renders the same `@embedding` serialization without processing any incoming parameters. The frontend calls `embedding.update({})` which triggers a PUT to this endpoint, but no data is persisted. This could cause confusion or mask missing functionality. Either implement actual update logic or remove the route/action to avoid a misleading API.

true_positives.golden_comment: logic: Potential nil pointer exception - if no TopicUser record exists, tu will be nil and calling methods on it will crash
true_positives.matched_candidate:
unsubscribe crashes when no TopicUser row exists

TopicUser.find_by(user_id: current_user.id, topic_id: params[:topic_id]) may return nil for users who received a notification (for example a mention, reply, or quote) without ever having a topic_users row. The next lines dereference tu.notification_level, causing NoMethodError. Use TopicUser.change(...) or find_or_initialize_by and handle the missing record, otherwise the unsubscribe page 500s for valid users.

false_negatives.golden_comment: Typo in property name: 'stopNotificiationsText' should be 'stopNotificationsText' (missing 'n' in 'Notifications')

false_positives.candidate:
Direct tu.save! bypasses TopicUser.change bookkeeping

Changing notification_level directly and calling save! does not set notifications_reason_id or notifications_changed_at, and does not publish the /topic/:id MessageBus update that TopicUser.change performs. Other live clients won't see the state change, and notification-change history/reasoning can become inconsistent. Use TopicUser.change(current_user.id, topic_id, notification_level: ...) instead.

Unsubscribe is a state-changing GET without CSRF or unique token

The new /t/:slug/:topic_id/unsubscribe and /t/:topic_id/unsubscribe routes are GET and directly change the user's notification_level. GET requests are not CSRF-protected and are treated as safe by clients, so a logged-in user can be unsubscribed by an embedded image, link prefetch, or email scanner following the URL. State changes should be POST/PUT with CSRF protection, or the link should include an unguessable per-user token.

Unsubscribe renders stale serialized topic notification state

@topic_view is constructed at line 99 before tu.notification_level is changed. perform_show_response then serializes that original @topic_view, so the preloaded JSON/HTML response contains the old notification level. The client's topic-notifications-button can show the pre-unsubscribe state, and another GET may be required to see the change. Rebuild @topic_view or update its topic-user data after saving.

Unsubscribe template path does not match topicUnsubscribe route name

This template is stored at templates/topic/unsubscribe.hbs, which Ember resolves for a nested topic.unsubscribe route. However app-route-map.js.es6 registers the route as top-level topicUnsubscribe, so Ember will look for templates/topic-unsubscribe.hbs. As a result the unsubscribe route will render without its intended template (empty or missing template), so the new unsubscribe page is broken.

unsubscribe_link translation now requires unsubscribe_url for all add_unsubscribe_link emails

The shared unsubscribe_link text now interpolates %{unsubscribe_url}. Email::MessageBuilder calls I18n.t('unsubscribe_link', template_args) for every message that sets add_unsubscribe_link: true, but only UserNotifications#send_notification_email has been updated in this diff to pass unsubscribe_url. Any other email using add_unsubscribe_link will now raise I18n::MissingInterpolationArgument or render a broken link. Either provide a default for unsubscribe_url, make the topic-specific sentence conditional, or update every caller.

true_positives.golden_comment: BlockedEmail.should_block_email? method has side effects during a read operation - it updates statistics even when just checking if an email should be blocked. This could cause race conditions in concurrent environments and makes the method name misleading.
true_positives.matched_candidate:
Non-atomic match_count increment and DB write inside validator

BlockedEmail.should_block? increments match_count and saves the record on every call. This method is invoked from EmailValidator during User validation, which can run multiple times per signup (e.g., user.valid? before save, then again during save). Each validation attempt will increment match_count multiple times, leading to inaccurate statistics. Concurrent signup attempts with the same blocked email will also suffer from lost updates because the increment is not atomic (no lock or update_all). This causes race conditions and corrupts match_count data. The method should either be split into a pure predicate and a separate tracking method, or use atomic increments (e.g., increment!(:match_count, touch: :last_match_at) with a transaction).

false_negatives.golden_comment: The regex pattern @(#{domains}) in email_in_restriction_setting? method only matches domain suffixes, not full domains with proper boundary anchoring. An attacker can register evil.example.com to bypass a whitelist entry for example.com.

The case-sensitive email lookup in `BlockedEmail.should_block?` creates a bypass risk, allowing 'User@Example.com' to bypass a block on 'user@example.com'. This can lead to unauthorized access to blocked users.

false_positives.candidate:
No tests for domain whitelist/blacklist logic in EmailValidator

The new EmailValidator replaces the previous email_validator method in User, which handled email domain whitelist and blacklist restrictions. The spec file only tests blocked email behavior, leaving the whitelist/blacklist logic untested. If a regression were introduced in that logic, no test would catch it. Tests should be added to verify that whitelist and blacklist settings correctly add or don't add errors to the email attribute.

true_positives.golden_comment: The current origin validation using indexOf is insufficient and can be bypassed. An attacker could use a malicious domain like evil-discourseUrl.com to pass this check.
true_positives.matched_candidate:
Substring check for message origin allows attacker-controlled origins

The condition `discourseUrl.indexOf(e.origin) === -1` tests whether the message origin contains the discourseUrl as a substring, rather than exact origin equality. An attacker could host a page on an origin such as `https://discourse.example.com.attacker.com` (which contains the legitimate origin as a substring) and send a postMessage to the embedding page. The check would incorrectly accept the message, allowing the attacker to trigger the resize handler and manipulate the iframe height, bypassing the intended origin restriction. The check should compare `e.origin` to the exact origin of `discourseUrl` using `new URL(discourseUrl).origin`.

true_positives.golden_comment: The ERB block closes with end if, which is invalid Ruby/ERB and will raise at render; it should just be end to close the if block.
true_positives.matched_candidate:
Invalid ERB syntax '<%- end if %>' causes template compile error

Line 6 contains '<%- end if %>', which is not valid ERB. The 'if' after 'end' is a syntax error; the conditional should be closed with '<%- end %>'. This will cause the view to fail to compile and result in a 500 error whenever the embed/best template is rendered.

true_positives.golden_comment: An unescaped request header (request.referer) is interpolated into JavaScript without proper escaping, which can lead to XSS vulnerabilities if the referer contains malicious content. This issue can allow attackers to execute arbitrary scripts in the context of the application.
true_positives.matched_candidate:
Unescaped referer in inline JavaScript allows XSS in Discourse origin

The line `parent.postMessage({type: 'discourse-resize', height: document['body'].offsetHeight}, '<%= request.referer %>');` inserts the raw request referer directly into a JavaScript string without escaping. An attacker who controls the embedding page's URL (which is allowed by the embeddable_host check) can include a single quote and arbitrary JavaScript payload that will execute in the context of the Discourse-origin iframe. This is a stored/reflected XSS vulnerability. The referer must be escaped using a JavaScript-safe method such as `j(request.referer)` or `escape_javascript`.

false_negatives.golden_comment: The PollFeed job calls open(SiteSetting.feed_polling_url) without validating the URL, allowing an attacker who controls the feed_polling_url site setting to make the server fetch arbitrary internal or external URLs.
postMessage targetOrigin should be the origin (scheme+host+port), not the full referrer URL; using the full URL will cause the message to be dropped and prevent resizing.

The code sets X-Frame-Options: ALLOWALL which completely disables clickjacking protection. The referer validation can be bypassed (referer headers are easily spoofed), and the fallback to empty string for nil referer masks validation failures.

The TopicEmbed.import method is susceptible to a NoMethodError if the contents parameter is nil when attempting to append a string, and an XSS vulnerability due to unescaped url interpolation in the generated HTML.

Calling `i.content.scrub` assumes that `i.content` is always populated. However, many RSS feeds do not provide a `content` field, leading to a potential nil pointer exception when `i.content` is nil. A fallback to `description` should be implemented to prevent crashes.

false_positives.candidate:
RSS/Atom feed content imported as raw HTML without sanitization

The `poll_feed` method extracts `i.content` from the feed and passes it directly to `TopicEmbed.import`, which stores the post with `cook_method = Post.cook_methods[:raw_html]`. Since raw HTML posts bypass all rendering and sanitization pipelines, any `<script>` or other malicious markup in the feed will be stored and served to users viewing the topic, leading to stored XSS. The feed content must be sanitized (e.g., with Sanitize or by using the regular markdown cooking path) before import.

Race condition in TopicEmbed.import can cause unique constraint violation

The `import` method first checks if a TopicEmbed exists for the URL, then creates a new one inside a transaction. If two processes invoke `import` simultaneously for the same URL, both may see no existing record, both create a new topic and post, and then both attempt to create a TopicEmbed with the same `embed_url`. The second `TopicEmbed.create!` will raise an ActiveRecord::RecordNotUnique exception due to the unique index on embed_url, causing the entire transaction (including the newly created topic and post) to be rolled back. The job will fail and the URL will remain unimported. A safer approach is to handle the unique violation gracefully (e.g., rescue and re-fetch) or use a database-level upsert/lock.

Unbounded open() in import_remote can hang or consume excessive resources

`TopicEmbed.import_remote` uses `open(url).read` without any timeout or size limit. A slow or unresponsive server could cause the job to hang indefinitely, tying up a worker, or a huge page could consume excessive memory. Consider using a library with timeouts and response size limits, or setting timeouts via open-uri options.

false_negatives.golden_comment: Mixing float: left with flexbox causes layout issues. -ms-align-items never existed in any version of IE/Edge; the correct legacy property is -ms-flex-align.
-webkit-box-ordinal-group and -moz-box-ordinal-group require values starting from 1, not 0. If $val is 0, this will cause incorrect rendering in older browsers, leading to layout issues.

With default `justify-content: flex-start` and no `margin-left: auto` on the button, the button is laid out immediately after `.small-action-desc` instead of on the right. Add `margin-left: auto` (or otherwise justify the item) to preserve the previous right alignment.

align-items mixin missing -moz-box-align for legacy Firefox

The `flexbox()` mixin emits `display: -moz-box`, so old Firefox builds that use it expect alignment through `-moz-box-align`, but `align-items()` only emits `-webkit-box-align`, `-ms-flex-align`, and the modern properties. In those browsers this change silently fails to center/baseline-align flex items. Add `-moz-box-align: $alignment` alongside `-webkit-box-align`.

true_positives.golden_comment: The include_website_name method is missing the required ? suffix. Rails serializers expect include_ methods to end with ? for conditional attribute inclusion, a convention followed by other methods in this serializer. Without it, the website_name attribute may not be conditionally included as intended. Additionally, the '.' << website_host string concatenation should be replaced with '.' + website_host or '.#{website_host}' to avoid mutating string literals, which can lead to issues.
true_positives.matched_candidate:
Inclusion predicate is missing the trailing question mark

`include_website_name` is defined without the trailing `?`, while serializer inclusion predicates in this file follow the `include_email?` / `include_website_name?` convention. As written, this method is not used as the inclusion check, so `website_name` can be emitted even when `website` is blank (as a null field) instead of being omitted. false_positives.candidate:
Derived website_name bypasses untrusted attribute filtering

`website_name` is added as a normal serialized attribute, but `website` is already in the `untrusted_attributes` list (lines 105-111), which suppresses fields for restricted users such as TL0 profiles viewed by anonymous visitors. Because `website_name` is derived from `website` and is not added to that untrusted list, it is still serialized and rendered when `website` itself would be hidden, leaking the user-supplied website host and path. Add `:website_name` to `untrusted_attributes` and add a spec asserting it is omitted alongside `website`.

Sibling-subdomain branch is not tested

The new `website_name` serializer logic has distinct branches for exact host match, same-length subdomain siblings (e.g. `www.example.com` vs `forum.example.com`), and parent-domain suffix matching. The new examples cover exact host and parent-domain cases but not the sibling-subdomain `elsif` branch, so a regression in that branch would not fail these tests. Add a spec using two different subdomains of the same parent domain.

true_positives.golden_comment: The `sendAddGuestsEmails` function does not check the `disableStandardEmails` flags in the `EventType` metadata, which may result in sending emails to hosts/attendees even when standard emails are disabled for the event type.

Calendar update uses requesting user's credentials instead of organizer's

If the caller is an attendee or a team admin who is not the organizer, `eventManager.updateCalendarAttendees(evt, booking)` will attempt to update the external calendar using the wrong credentials, likely failing to update the organizer's calendar and potentially modifying the caller's calendar with an event they do not own. Error toast prepends error code but translation may be incorrect

If this endpoint is invoked concurrently by overlapping cron runs, two attempts can both read `retryCount: 0` and both write `retryCount: 1`, so two failures are counted as one. The reminder may then be retried indefinitely instead of deleted after two failures. Use Prisma's atomic `retryCount: { increment: 1 }` instead of setting it from the stale value.

Missing sendTo or empty message never increments retry count

The retry count is only incremented when `twilio.scheduleSMS` is actually called and fails or throws. If `message` is empty or `sendTo` is missing/falsy, the reminder is skipped entirely, remains `scheduled: false`, and retains the same `retryCount`. Such reminders will be selected forever on every cron run, which is the exact repeated-scheduling problem this PR is meant to fix. Post-schedule DB failure is counted as SMS scheduling failure

After two such failures the reminder is deleted even though an SMS is already scheduled on Twilio. The retry count should only be incremented for failures from the actual scheduling call, not for failures while updating the result record.

The org scope test expects the `Prisma.sql` condition to contain the array `[testData.org.id, testData.team.id, team2.id, team3.id]` in that exact order. Workflow reminder cancellations are not awaited

`updatedBookings.forEach` starts `deleteScheduledEmailReminder` and `deleteScheduledSMSReminder` but does not `await` them or collect their promises. This API handler returns right after `sendCancelledEmails`, so the process can end before the async Prisma update/delete or provider cancellation completes. true_positives.golden_comment: When immediateDelete is true, the deleteScheduledEmailReminder function cancels the SendGrid email but fails to delete the corresponding WorkflowReminder record from the database. Immediate email cancellation leaves stale scheduled reminders in the database

With `immediateDelete` true and a `referenceId`, this function sends the SendGrid cancel and returns without deleting or marking the `WorkflowReminder`. The reschedule path in `handleNewBooking` calls it this way and does not delete the row afterwards, leaving the old reminder as `scheduled: true` with `cancelled` null. false_positives.candidate:
Disabling event types does not await reminder cancellation

`remindersToDelete.flat().forEach(...)` invokes cancellation functions without awaiting their promises. Disabling an event type from a workflow can return to the client before the email reminder row is updated to `cancelled: true` or the SMS reminder is deleted. If the runtime shuts down after the response, the cancellation is lost and reminders for disabled workflows can still send. The same fire-and-forget pattern appears below when deleting/editing steps; all cancellation promises should be awaited before returning.

Non-immediate email cancellation waits for cron and can miss the send window

When called without `immediateDelete`, this function only sets `cancelled: true` in the database and returns; it never calls SendGrid to cancel the scheduled send. Callers like `handleCancelBooking` and `requestReschedule` use this path for all email reminders. Because `scheduleEmailReminders` runs only every 15 minutes, a reminder whose `scheduledDate` is before the next cron run will already have been sent by SendGrid before the cron attempts cancellation. Cancelling a booking close to a reminder time can therefore still deliver the reminder. For reminders within the near-term window, SendGrid should be cancelled immediately or the cancellation must be event-driven.

Old reminders are cancelled before rescheduling succeeds

This block sends cancellation for `originalRescheduledBooking.workflowReminders` before `eventManager.reschedule` runs. If the reschedule fails, for example due to a calendar or video integration error, the original booking remains active but its workflow reminders have already been cancelled. A live booking would then stop receiving reminders. Move this cancellation to after a successful reschedule, or compensate on failure if it must occur before.

One SendGrid cancellation failure aborts all remaining cancellations in the cron run

The entire `for` loop is inside one `try`/`catch`. If `client.request` throws for one reminder, execution jumps to the catch, skipping every remaining `remindersToCancel` entry and never awaiting the already-created Prisma delete promises. A single persistently bad `referenceId` or transient SendGrid error can block all other due cancellations in that run. Handle each reminder's SendGrid cancellation and delete independently (or continue on error) so one failure cannot prevent the rest.

Request-reschedule reminder cancellation is fire-and-forget

The `requestReschedule` mutation calls `deleteScheduledEmailReminder` and `deleteScheduledSMSReminder` inside `forEach` without awaiting their promises. In a serverless/TRPC context the mutation can resolve before the DB rows are marked or deleted and before Twilio/SendGrid operations finish, so reminders for the cancelled original booking can survive and still send. Collect and await these promises before the mutation returns.

true_positives.golden_comment: The code uses forEach with async callbacks, which causes asynchronous operations (e.g., calendar/video event deletions, payment refunds) to run concurrently without being awaited. This 'fire-and-forget' behavior leads to unhandled promise rejections, race conditions, and incomplete cleanup, as surrounding try-catch blocks cannot properly handle errors from these unawaited promises. Replace forEach with for...of loops or Promise.all() with map() to ensure proper sequential execution and error handling.
true_positives.matched_candidate:
forEach(async) does not await deletion operations

The change to `forEach(async (bookingRef) => { ... await getCalendar(...); return calendar?.deleteEvent(...) })` does not cause the loop to wait for the async callbacks. The async operations (calendar event deletion or video meeting deletion) are fire-and-forget, and the surrounding function continues execution and returns `true` before these deletions complete. This can lead to a race condition where the reschedule email is sent and the function returns success while the external calendar/video events are still being deleted (or have failed). Use a `for...of` loop with `await` or collect promises and `await Promise.all`.

false_negatives.golden_comment: Consider adding try-catch around the await to handle import failures gracefully

false_positives.candidate:
Ineffective await on array of promises in paid cancellation path

In the paid cancellation branch, the code executes `await apiDeletes;` where `apiDeletes` is an array containing Promises from `deleteMeeting` and `calendar?.deleteEvent`. `await` on an array does not await the individual promises; it simply yields the array. Therefore, the function does not wait for these asynchronous deletion operations to complete before marking the booking as REJECTED and returning. This can lead to inconsistent state (e.g., booking marked rejected while external calendar event still exists). Use `await Promise.all(apiDeletes)` instead.

Recurring cancellation forEach is not awaited and pushes resolved values

In the recurring booking cancellation branch, the code uses `forEach(async (credential) => { ... const deletedEvent = await calendar?.deleteEvent(...); apiDeletes.push(deletedEvent); })`. The `forEach` does not wait for these async callbacks, and because `deletedEvent` is the resolved value (not a Promise), `apiDeletes` contains non-promise values that `Promise.all` later will not wait for. The function can proceed to send emails and return success before the external calendar events are actually deleted. Use a `for...of` loop and collect the promises returned by `calendar?.deleteEvent` without awaiting them inside the loop, or use `Promise.all` on an array of promises.

forEach(async) does not await calendar/video deletion before sending email

The code at line 553 uses `bookingRefsFiltered.forEach(async (bookingRef) => { ... const calendar = await getCalendar(...); return calendar?.deleteEvent(...) })`. Because the callback is async but the `forEach` does not await it, the deletion promises are not collected or awaited. The function immediately proceeds to send the reschedule email, potentially before the external calendar/video events have been cancelled. Use a `for...of` loop with `await` or collect the promises and `await Promise.all`.

forEach(async) does not await deletion operations

Same issue as in vital/lib/reschedule.ts: `bookingRefsFiltered.forEach(async (bookingRef) => { ... await getCalendar(...); return calendar?.deleteEvent(...) })` does not await the async callbacks, so the calendar/video deletion operations are not awaited before the function returns `true`. This can cause incomplete cancellation and inconsistent state.

getCalendarCredentials returns unresolved Promises for calendar

`getCalendarCredentials` is a synchronous function that calls the now-async `getCalendar(credential)` without awaiting it. As a result, each returned object's `calendar` property is a Promise, not a Calendar instance. While some consumers (e.g., `getConnectedCalendars`) correctly await this promise, other callers of `getCalendarCredentials` may not, leading to unawaited promises or runtime errors when trying to call calendar methods. The function should either become async and await `getCalendar`, or its return type should be explicitly documented and all consumers updated to await the calendar promise.

true_positives.golden_comment: Incorrect end time calculation using slotStartTime instead of slotEndTime
true_positives.matched_candidate:
Working hours check uses slot start for both start and end and ignores timezone

In the working-hours validation added to `checkIfIsAvailable`, `const start` and `const end` are both set to `slotStartTime.hour() * 60 + slotStartTime.minute()`. This means the check never accounts for the event length, and also uses the slot's UTC time directly without converting to the organizer's timezone. Working hours are defined in the organizer's local time. As a result, valid slots may be rejected or invalid slots allowed for any non-UTC timezone. The check should compare the slot's start and end times (in the organizer's timezone) against the working hour boundaries.

false_negatives.golden_comment: Using === for dayjs object comparison will always return false as it compares object references, not values. Use .isSame() method instead: dayjs(date.start).add(utcOffset, 'minutes').isSame(dayjs(date.end).add(utcOffset, minutes))

false_positives.candidate:
Date override logic marks partially overlapping slots as available

In `checkIfIsAvailable`, the date override check only rejects slots that are entirely before the override start or entirely after the override end (by checking `slotEndTime.isBefore(start)` / `slotEndTime.isSame(start)` and `slotStartTime.isAfter(end)`). A slot that starts before the override start but ends inside the override window will not be rejected and will be considered available. Since a date override replaces normal working hours, any slot not fully contained in the override should be unavailable. This can lead to bookings being offered that begin before the host's available time.

Date override start/end minutes are computed in UTC instead of invitee timezone

The code computes `startTime` and `endTime` as `dayjs(override.start).utc().add(offset, "minute").hour() * 60 + ...`. This keeps the time in UTC (after shifting by offset) and extracts hour/minute without converting to the invitee's timezone. The resulting minutes are relative to UTC midnight, not to the invitee's local midnight, which is what `buildSlots` expects. This produces incorrect slot times whenever the invitee timezone is not UTC. The correct implementation is to use `dayjs(override.start).tz(timeZone).hour()*60 + dayjs(override.start).tz(timeZone).minute()` (and similarly for end). This bug affects all events with date overrides and a non-UTC invitee timezone.

Incorrect organizer UTC offset calculation uses Date.toString()

`dayjs(override.start.toString()).tz(override.timeZone)` first converts the Date to a string in the environment's local timezone, then interprets that string as if it were in `override.timeZone`. This changes the instant. For example, if the server runs in UTC, a Date representing 14:00 IST would be converted to an 08:30 UTC string, and then parsed as 08:30 IST, completely shifting the time. The correct approach is `dayjs(override.start).tz(override.timeZone).utcOffset()`. This bug causes date override windows to be placed at wrong times for all users when the server timezone differs from the organizer's timezone.

Missing test for round-robin fixed host date overrides

The PR description states it fixes date overrides for fixed hosts in round-robin events, but the only added test is for a personal event with a different attendee timezone. There is no test covering the round-robin scenario where a fixed host has a date override and a non-fixed host is available. Without such a test, the core bug fix is unverified and could regress silently.

UTC offset for date override is computed incorrectly

`const utcOffset = organizerTimeZone ? dayjs.tz(date.start, organizerTimeZone).utcOffset() * -1 : 0;` treats `date.start` (an absolute Date object) as if it were a local time string in `organizerTimeZone`. This computes the wrong offset and causes the subsequent day comparison (`dayjs(date.start).add(utcOffset, "minutes").format("YYYY MM DD")`) to potentially match the wrong day. The correct approach is to directly format `date.start` in the organizer's timezone using `dayjs(date.start).tz(organizerTimeZone).format("YYYY MM DD")` without any manual offset manipulation.

false_positives.candidate:
GitHub user validation is skipped for first-time installs

When `Integration.objects.get(external_id=installation_id)` raises `DoesNotExist`, `GitHubInstallation.dispatch` returns `pipeline.next_step()` immediately, before the `github_authenticated_user` vs `integration.metadata["sender"]["login"]` comparison at lines 500-505. `build_integration` also only records `sender` if it was already present in pipeline state, so a normal first installation creates an integration with no sender metadata. false_positives.candidate:
Graceful shutdown stops the commit loop before draining and committing queued work

`close()` sets `shutdown_event` and joins `commit_thread` before `queue_pool.shutdown()` drains queued work. Messages completed during pool shutdown therefore have no commit loop left to commit them. Additionally, `FixedQueuePool.shutdown` sets each worker's `shutdown` flag before calling `q.shutdown(immediate=False)`, so a worker woken from `get()` processes at most one more item and then exits the `while not self.shutdown` loop, leaving the rest of the queue undrained. The result is that successfully processed messages near shutdown may not be committed, causing duplicate reprocessing after restart (and making `wait_until_empty` unused despite existing for this purpose).

Offsets are completed even when result processing fails

In `OrderedQueueWorker.run`, `self.offset_tracker.complete_offset(...)` is in the `finally` block. If `result_processor` raises, the offset is still marked completed and can be committed by `_commit_loop`. This contradicts the strategy's guarantee that offsets are only committed after successful processing: a transient or programming failure can cause the message to be lost forever once Kafka commits past it. The same commit-on-error behavior exists in `SimpleQueueProcessingStrategy.submit`'s broad exception handler. `complete_offset` should only be called on successful processing, or failed items must be explicitly marked as non-committable.

Queue pool is shut down by the per-assignment strategy and then reused after rebalance

`ResultsStrategyFactory` creates one `FixedQueuePool` and stores it on the factory. Arroyo can call `create_with_partitions` again on this same factory after a partition assignment/rebalance. However, `SimpleQueueProcessingStrategy.close()` calls `self.queue_pool.shutdown()`, which permanently shuts down the queues and worker threads owned by the factory. On the next assignment, `create_with_partitions` reuses the already-shutdown pool. New submits will call `put()` on a shutdown queue, raise `queue.ShutDown`, be caught by the broad `except` in `SimpleQueueProcessingStrategy.submit`, and the offset will still be marked complete. This means messages are dropped and their Kafka offsets are advanced without processing after any rebalance. The queue pool should either be created per assignment or `close()` must not shut down the factory-owned pool.

Unbounded queues provide no backpressure and can exhaust memory

Each per-group queue is created as `queue.Queue()` with the default `maxsize=0`, meaning it is unbounded. The class docstring claims "natural backpressure when queues fill up," but because the queues never fill, the Kafka polling thread will keep enqueueing items for a slow group without bound. Under sustained slowness or a stalled subscription, this can grow memory until the consumer process is OOM-killed. Use bounded queues or otherwise block/stop polling when queue depth exceeds a configured threshold.

Uses queue.Queue.shutdown / queue.ShutDown, which are Python 3.13+ APIs

`Queue.shutdown()` and `queue.ShutDown` were added in Python 3.13. On Python 3.11/3.12 runtimes, `FixedQueuePool.shutdown` reaches `q.shutdown(immediate=False)`, which raises `AttributeError`; that is caught and logged, but workers are never unblocked with a `ShutDown` exception. The thread-queue-parallel consumer can then hang on shutdown until each worker join times out. This feature must either avoid these APIs or the runtime baseline and CI matrix must be explicitly upgraded to Python 3.13+.

Consequently, subsequent logs in the Delete method (including errors from Storage.Delete) will lack these contextual fields, making debugging harder. It should be ctx = klog.NewContext(ctx, log).

true_positives.golden_comment: Inconsistency: using name instead of options.Kind for metrics recording differs from other methods.
true_positives.matched_candidate:
Multiple metrics are recorded under the wrong name or store

Several metric calls are incorrect: in Create error path (line 45) records legacy duration instead of storage; in Update error path (line 129) records legacy duration instead of storage; in Delete success path (line 106) passes the resource name as the 'kind' label instead of options.Kind; in DeleteCollection goroutine (line 166) records storage duration for the legacy operation instead of legacy duration. These errors cause Prometheus metrics to be mislabeled or attributed to the wrong store, leading to incorrect monitoring and alerting. All timing and label arguments must be corrected to reflect the actual operation being measured.

false_negatives.golden_comment: In DualWriterMode3's DeleteCollection method, when a storage operation fails, recordStorageDuration is incorrectly called with recordLegacyDuration instead.

false_positives.candidate:
Async legacy writes use the request-scoped context and will be canceled immediately

In Create (lines 50-56), Delete (108-113), Update (134-140), and DeleteCollection (161-166), the goroutine creates a timeout context from the request context (ctx). When the HTTP handler returns, its context is typically canceled. The goroutine's legacy write then inherits this canceled context and is aborted before completing. This defeats the purpose of asynchronous fallback writes: the legacy store will almost never receive the write. The code should use a context detached from the request (e.g., context.Background() with timeout) while preserving any necessary values (like authentication).

Integration tests for mode 3 may be flaky due to asynchronous legacy writes

The added subtests for mode 3 (file and unified storage) run the same doPlaylistTests which immediately checks legacy API results after k8s API operations. Since mode 3 writes to legacy asynchronously, there is no guarantee that the legacy write has completed before the test queries the legacy endpoint. This can cause intermittent failures (e.g., legacy list missing the just-created playlist). The test needs a synchronization mechanism or a polling wait to ensure the async write has propagated before asserting on the legacy API.

Legacy Create receives the original input object, not the object persisted in unified storage

In Create, the goroutine passes `obj` (the original input) to Legacy.Create, ignoring the `created` object returned by Storage.Create. Unified storage typically applies defaulting, assigns UID, resourceVersion, and creationTimestamp. The legacy store will therefore receive an object missing these modifications, leading to data inconsistency between the two stores. The code should pass `created` (or a sanitized copy) to the legacy write to ensure both stores reflect the same final state.

Legacy update uses the original objInfo instead of the object updated in unified storage

In Update, after d.Storage.Update succeeds, the goroutine calls d.Legacy.Update with the same objInfo that was passed to the unified storage call. The previous implementation used an updateWrapper to reuse the already computed updated object. Without it, Legacy.Update will invoke objInfo.UpdatedObject against the legacy store's own old object, which may differ (e.g., missing new fields, different resourceVersion). This can cause the legacy write to produce a different object or fail validation, breaking the dual-write guarantee. The code should pass a wrapper or the object returned by Storage.Update to ensure both stores persist the same data.

Removal of local prometheus registry causes duplicate metric registration panic

The diff removes `p := prometheus.NewRegistry()` from TestMode1_Get, causing it to use the package-level global `p` (var p = prometheus.NewRegistry()). If NewDualWriter registers metrics on the provided registry (as dualWriterMetrics likely does using promauto), then the first test that uses the global registry (e.g., TestMode1_Create) will register metrics, and any subsequent test using the same global registry will panic with duplicate metric registration. This will break the entire test package. Each test should create and use its own fresh prometheus registry, or the global registry must be reset between tests.

Tests for asynchronous legacy writes do not wait for completion and ignore mock expectations

Multiple tests (e.g., TestMode3_Create, TestMode3_Delete, TestMode3_Update) set up legacy mock expectations but never call m.AssertExpectations() and do not wait for the goroutine to finish. The test may pass even if the legacy write is never called or fails, and the mock call may occur after the test completes, causing race conditions or panics if the legacy method is not stubbed. This prevents any verification of the asynchronous dual-write behavior and can lead to flaky or silently failing tests. The tests must synchronize with the goroutine (e.g., using a WaitGroup or a done channel) and assert expectations before finishing.

true_positives.golden_comment: The GetWebAssets function implements an incomplete double-checked locking pattern for caching web assets. The function first checks if the cache is populated using a read lock (RLock), and if the cache is empty, it acquires a write lock to populate it. However, it fails to re-check whether the cache was populated by another goroutine while waiting to acquire the write lock.
true_positives.matched_candidate:
Double-checked locking missing re-check after acquiring write lock

GetWebAssets releases the read lock at line 43 and later acquires the write lock at line 48, but after acquiring the write lock it does not re-read entryPointAssetsCache before doing the expensive load. If many goroutines call concurrently when the cache is nil (e.g. the first requests in production), all of them will see nil under RLock, block on Lock, and then sequentially reload the manifest from file/CDN and overwrite the cache. The cache is not single-flight; this can cause a thundering herd of disk/network reads and JSON parsing at startup. Add a second cache check immediately after acquiring the write lock (e.g. if cfg.Env != setting.Dev && entryPointAssetsCache != nil { return entryPointAssetsCache, nil }) before loading.

false_negatives.golden_comment: In addition to the missing double-check, the function has a critical flaw in its error handling: it unconditionally assigns the fetch result to the cache (line 69: entryPointAssetsCache = result) regardless of whether the fetch succeeded or failed. When an error occurs during asset fetching, result is nil, and this nil value overwrites any previously valid cache entry.

false_positives.candidate:
No test for concurrent access or caching behavior

This change modifies only webassets.go and adds synchronization around the global cache, but no test is added that exercises concurrent calls to GetWebAssets (e.g. under -race) or verifies that non-Dev callers reuse the cached value and that concurrent startup loads are handled correctly. A regression test would help confirm the data race is actually fixed and would reveal the duplicate-load issue described above.

true_positives.golden_comment: The enableSqlExpressions function has flawed logic that always returns false, effectively disabling SQL expressions unconditionally:
true_positives.matched_candidate:
enableSqlExpressions always returns false and contains dead code

The function `enableSqlExpressions` is misleading: it checks the `sqlExpressions` feature flag but ignores the result and always returns `false`. The logic `enabled := !h.features.IsEnabledGlobally(...); if enabled { return false } return false` is equivalent to `return false`. This dead code suggests the flag can enable the feature, which is not the case after this security fix. It should be simplified to `return false` with a comment explaining the feature is permanently disabled, or the function removed entirely.

false_negatives.golden_comment: The DB methods NewInMemoryDB().RunCommands, DB.QueryFramesInto, and DB.TablesList in pkg/expr/sql/db.go return hardcoded 'not implemented' errors after removing the go-duck dependency.

false_positives.candidate:
No tests for disabled SQL expressions or stub DB

This PR disables SQL expressions for security reasons and replaces the DuckDB-backed implementation with a stub that always returns "not implemented". However, no unit tests were added or updated to verify that (1) `ReadQuery` returns an error for `QueryTypeSQL` regardless of the feature flag, and (2) the stub DB methods (`TablesList`, `RunCommands`, `QueryFramesInto`) always return the expected error. For a security-critical change, test coverage is important to prevent accidental regression that could re-enable the vulnerable feature.

true_positives.golden_comment: A race condition in BuildIndex allows multiple goroutines to concurrently build the same expensive index for the same key. This is caused by moving the b.cacheMu lock from protecting the entire function to only protecting the final cache assignment.
true_positives.matched_candidate:
Concurrent BuildIndex for the same key can cause file index creation errors

Removing the global cacheMu.Lock from BuildIndex means two goroutines can now concurrently build an index for the same NamespacedResource. getOrCreateIndex does not provide per-key mutual exclusion (see TODO at resource/search.go lines 288-290), so concurrent search requests for the same resource will both see a nil index and call BuildIndex. For file-based indexes (size > FileThreshold), both goroutines will call bleve.New on the same directory path, which is not safe and can fail with an error such as 'index already exists' or corrupt the index. For memory indexes, both will build identical indexes and the last insertion wins, wasting work. Need per-key locking or singleflight to prevent duplicate concurrent builds.

true_positives.golden_comment: Calling s.search.TotalDocs() here may race with concurrent index creation: TotalDocs iterates b.cache without synchronization, and the event watcher goroutine started just above could trigger BuildIndex writes concurrently, potentially causing a concurrent map read/write panic.
true_positives.matched_candidate:
TotalDocs reads the cache map without holding RLock

TotalDocs iterates over b.cache without acquiring b.cacheMu.RLock. With the reduced locking in BuildIndex, cache is now written concurrently by any call to BuildIndex (e.g., from getOrCreateIndex on search requests) while TotalDocs may be called (for example, in searchSupport.init at resource/search.go line 216 or externally). This constitutes a concurrent map read/write and will cause a runtime panic or map corruption. TotalDocs must take cacheMu.RLock, or the cache must be otherwise synchronized.

false_positives.candidate:
Cancel function not called when Init fails during NewResourceServer

NewResourceServer creates a cancellable context and stores its cancel function in the server struct. If s.Init(ctx) returns an error, the function logs and returns nil, err without calling s.cancel(). Any goroutines started during Init (e.g., from lifecycle.Init or WatchWriteEvents in search.init) may continue running with no way to be stopped, leaking resources. The cancel should be invoked before returning the error.

Data race on totalBatchesIndexed in concurrent errgroup goroutines

Inside s.init, totalBatchesIndexed++ is executed by multiple goroutines running under an errgroup with SetLimit(s.initWorkers). The variable is not protected by a mutex or atomic operation and is later read after group.Wait() to add a span event. This is a data race and can produce incorrect counts or be flagged by the race detector.

Gap between index build and watch start can miss write events

In searchSupport.init, the index is built from a snapshot using ListIterator (lines 181-193), and only afterwards is WatchWriteEvents called to start the watcher (line 203). Any writes that occur between the snapshot read and the watcher's initialization will not be reflected in the newly built index, because the watcher starts after the build and does not replay missed events. This can lead to stale search results until the next event for that resource. The watcher should ideally be started before or atomically with the snapshot, or the backend should provide a mechanism to replay missed events.

Search watcher goroutine uses background context and does not handle closed channel

The searchSupport.init function starts WatchWriteEvents with watchctx := context.Background() rather than the cancellable ctx passed to init. This watcher goroutine will never be cancelled when the server stops, causing a goroutine leak. Additionally, the goroutine reads from the events channel without checking for closure; if the channel is closed (e.g., due to backend termination), the receive yields a nil *WrittenEvent, and handleEvent will dereference it in the slices.Contains call, causing a panic. The context should be tied to the server and the channel closure should be handled safely.

true_positives.golden_comment: Cleanup reference uses incorrect alias - should be 'idp-alias-' + i instead of 'alias'.
true_positives.matched_candidate:
Test cleanup uses literal "alias" instead of the actual alias variable

In both testCacheIDPByOrg and testCacheIDPForLogin, the cleanup registration `getCleanup().addCleanup(testRealm().identityProviders().get("alias")::remove);` passes the string "alias" instead of the loop variable `alias`. This means the created identity providers are not cleaned up after the test, leaving leftover data that can affect subsequent tests. It should be `testRealm().identityProviders().get(alias)::remove`.

false_negatives.golden_comment: InfinispanIdentityProviderStorageProvider.getForLogin() recursively calls session.identityProviders().getById() instead of idpDelegate.getById(), causing the cache lookup to re-enter the same caching layer.

false_positives.candidate:
Login cache is not invalidated when an organization is enabled or disabled

The getForLogin cache key is invalidated only in registerIDPLoginInvalidation and registerIDPLoginInvalidationOnUpdate, which are triggered by IDP create/update/remove. However, the login eligibility also depends on the organization's enabled state (enforced by the organization-aware wrapper added elsewhere). If an organization is disabled after the cache is populated, the cached login list still includes IDPs from that organization, potentially showing them on the login page or allowing them to be used for authentication by consumers that do not re-check isEnabled(). The cache should be invalidated when an organization's enabled state changes, but there is currently no mechanism to register such invalidation. This leads to stale, security-relevant data.

true_positives.golden_comment: Returns wrong provider (default keystore instead of BouncyCastle)
true_positives.matched_candidate:
getBouncyCastleProvider returns an unrelated default KeyStore provider

The CryptoProvider contract describes `getBouncyCastleProvider()` as returning the BouncyCastle (or FIPS BouncyCastle) provider. This implementation returns `KeyStore.getInstance(KeyStore.getDefaultType()).getProvider()`, which is normally a JDK provider such as SunJCE/SunJSSE and has no relation to BouncyCastle. Callers that rely on BC algorithms or provider identity will get incorrect behavior. Returning null, as WildFlyElytronProvider does, or actually loading/registering BouncyCastle would be consistent with the interface.

true_positives.golden_comment: Abstract order() method on CryptoProvider may break backward compatibility with existing implementations
true_positives.matched_candidate:
Adding abstract order() breaks binary compatibility for existing CryptoProvider implementations

CryptoProvider is a public interface that external integrations may implement and compile against older Keycloak versions. Adding an abstract method `int order()` makes existing provider JARs binary-incompatible: ServiceLoader will instantiate them, and the method reference `CryptoProvider::order` used in CryptoIntegration.detectProvider will throw AbstractMethodError because the implementation class lacks that method. Keep binary compatibility by making `order()` a default method, for example `default int order() { return 0; }`.

false_negatives.golden_comment: Dead code exists where ASN1Encoder instances are created and written to, but their results are immediately discarded. The actual encoding is performed by new ASN1Encoder instances created in the subsequent return statement, rendering the earlier operations useless.
When length starts at -1 from indefinite-length encoding, the arithmetic 'length = length - bytes.length' will behave unexpectedly, potentially leading to incorrect processing of encoded data.

false_positives.candidate:
Equal provider order values make provider selection nondeterministic

detectProvider now sorts providers only by `order` descending and silently picks the first one. DefaultCryptoProvider, WildFlyElytronProvider and FIPS1402Provider all return 200, and ServiceLoader encounter order for equal priority is not specified. If more than one of these providers is on the classpath, the selected crypto implementation becomes arbitrary and can change between runs or environments, replacing the previous fail-fast behavior. Assign distinct order values or add a deterministic tie-breaker.

Registered CryptoProvider throws UnsupportedOperationException for core signing operations

AuthzClientCryptoProvider is registered through META-INF/services and becomes the active CryptoProvider when no higher-order provider exists. However `getSignature` and many other required CryptoProvider methods throw UnsupportedOperationException. Keycloak's JWS signing path calls `CryptoIntegration.getProvider().getSignature(algorithm)`, so client authentication or token handling that requires signing will fail at runtime when this provider is selected. The added test only exercises ASN.1 conversion directly and does not exercise provider selection or JWS signing, so this regression is not covered. Either implement the needed methods or do not register this class as a general CryptoProvider.

readSequence can loop forever on a zero-length child element

`readSequence` loops while `length > 0` and decrements `length` by `bytes.length`. `readNext()` can return a zero-length byte array when a child TLV has content length 0, which is valid ASN.1 DER for some primitive types. If that happens, `length` is never decremented and this loop spins forever. The decoder is used to parse DER-encoded ECDSA signatures, so a malicious or malformed signature can cause CPU exhaustion or denial of service. Reject zero-length TLV children in this path or decrement by the number of header bytes consumed separately.

true_positives.golden_comment: Inconsistent feature flag bug causing orphaned permissions. The AdminPermissions event listener, responsible for cleaning up permissions upon role, client, or group removal, is incorrectly guarded by the ADMIN_FINE_GRAINED_AUTHZ (V1) feature flag. This is inconsistent with other methods in the class that use ADMIN_FINE_GRAINED_AUTHZ_V2. Consequently, if ADMIN_FINE_GRAINED_AUTHZ_V2 is enabled but V1 is not, the permission cleanup logic will not execute, leading to orphaned permission data. Cleanup should occur regardless of which fine-grained authorization version is enabled.
true_positives.matched_candidate:
Listener cleanup is gated on the wrong feature flag for V2

The event handling block is gated on Profile.Feature.ADMIN_FINE_GRAINED_AUTHZ (V1), but this PR is for ADMIN_FINE_GRAINED_AUTHZ_V2. When only V2 is enabled, removal events for roles, clients, and groups are ignored, so associated admin permission resources/policies are not cleaned up. Conversely, if both V1 and V2 are enabled, management() returns MgmtPermissionsV2 and clients().setPermissionsEnabled() throws UnsupportedOperationException, so client removal events can cause a server error. The check should use ADMIN_FINE_GRAINED_AUTHZ_V2, and the V2 evaluator must implement the cleanup path.

true_positives.golden_comment: In getClientsWithPermission(String scope), iterating resourceStore.findByType(server, AdminPermissionsSchema.CLIENTS_RESOURCE_TYPE) and returning resource.getName() will only ever consider the type-level 'Clients' resource (per-client resources have no type) and return its name, while AvailableRoleMappingResource#getRoleIdsWithPermissions expects actual client IDs to pass to realm.getClientById, which can lead to incorrect behavior or a null client and subsequent failures.
true_positives.matched_candidate:
getClientsWithPermission filters by a type that per-client resources do not have

resourceStore.findByType is called with AdminPermissionsSchema.CLIENTS_RESOURCE_TYPE, but per-client resources created by AdminPermissionsSchema.getOrCreateResource are created without calling setType, so they will not be returned by this query. The all-clients type resource itself does match and its name "Clients" is added to the result as if it were a client ID. As a result, the returned set does not contain the actual client IDs needed for admin list filtering, regardless of whether specific-client or all-client permissions are granted.

false_negatives.golden_comment: In hasPermission(ClientModel client, String scope), the resource lookup uses findByName(server, client.getId(), server.getId()), but AdminPermissionsSchema.getOrCreateResource creates per-client resources with the owner set to resourceServer.getClientId(), so this lookup will never find those resources and will always fall back to the 'all-clients' resource, effectively ignoring client-specific permissions.

In ClientPermissionsV2.hasPermission, the method getResourceTypeResource could return null, leading to a NullPointerException in findByResource. Defensive null checks are needed to prevent this issue.
Remove unused getEvaluationContext private method in ClientPermissionsV2 - it is defined but never called

false_positives.candidate:
getResourceName does not resolve client resources added in this PR

getResourceName only handles the Users resource type. Client-specific resources are named by the client UUID and are created without a display name, so for the newly added Clients resource type this method falls through to resource.getDisplayName() and returns a null or otherwise meaningless value. This breaks human-readable permission/resource descriptions for client resources. A CLIENTS branch should resolve the ClientModel and return its clientId, similar to the existing user branch.

false_negatives.golden_comment: Incorrect method call for exit codes. The picocli.exit() method calls System.exit() directly, which is problematic:
Need to add changelog/release notes documenting the exit code change and migration guidance

false_positives.candidate:
New exit codes 3 and 4 are not asserted by the CLI tests

The PR documents that recreate upgrades exit with code 3 and feature-disabled invocations exit with code 4, and `CompatibilityResult` now defines `RECREATE_UPGRADE_EXIT_CODE = 3` and `FEATURE_DISABLED = 4`. However, `testFeatureNotEnabled` only asserts the error text and `testWrongVersions` only asserts error messages; neither asserts `cliResult.exitCode()` equals 3 or 4. Also, the feature-disabled path is only tested for the `metadata` subcommand, not for `check`. A regression changing either exit code would not be detected by these tests.

Null update strategy case does not enable rolling-updates feature, but a test expects a rolling upgrade

`createInitialDeployment` returns at line 106 before enabling `Profile.Feature.ROLLING_UPDATES` when `updateStrategy` is null. `testCacheMaxCount` is parameterized with `null` and then expects `eventuallyRollingUpgradeStatus` for a configuration change. Since this PR introduces rolling-updates as a preview feature and documents that it must be enabled for operator update behavior, the null-strategy configuration-change case either fails if the operator enforces the feature flag, or does not exercise the feature-gated path if the operator still allows legacy rolling updates. The feature should be enabled for the null strategy when a rolling update is expected, or the expectation should be adjusted.

true_positives.golden_comment: In GroupPermissionsV2.canManage(), the permission fallback checks for both VIEW and MANAGE scopes (hasPermission(null, AdminPermissionsSchema.VIEW, AdminPermissionsSchema.MANAGE)), but canManage() should only grant access for MANAGE scope, not VIEW. This means users with only VIEW permission on groups can pass the canManage() check, granting them write access they should not have. The canView() method correctly checks both VIEW and MANAGE, but canManage() should only check MANAGE.
true_positives.matched_candidate:
VIEW permission on all groups grants manage access

GroupPermissionsV2.canManage() calls hasPermission(null, AdminPermissionsSchema.VIEW, AdminPermissionsSchema.MANAGE). This means that a caller with only the VIEW scope on all groups will be considered as having manage permission. As a result, any operation requiring requireManage(), such as creating groups, adding child groups, or updating groups, will be allowed without the MANAGE scope. The method should only check the MANAGE scope. This is a privilege escalation vulnerability.

true_positives.golden_comment: In getGroupIdsWithViewPermission, hasPermission is called with groupResource.getId() and the same groupResource.getId() is added to granted, but hasPermission resolves resources by name (treating the argument as a group id) and the GroupPermissionEvaluator contract says this method returns group IDs that are later used as UserModel.GROUPS and in getUsersCount group filters. This mismatch means per-group VIEW_MEMBERS/MANAGE_MEMBERS permissions may not yield the expected group IDs for filtering and counts, and evaluation may effectively only look at the type-level 'all-groups' resource; consider revisiting whether this should operate on the underlying group ids (resource names) instead so it aligns with the JPA queries and the interface contract.
true_positives.matched_candidate:
getGroupIdsWithViewPermission returns resource IDs instead of group IDs

In the callback of resourceStore.findByType, the method adds groupResource.getId() to the granted set. Resource.getId() is the internal authorization resource UUID, which is not the same as the group ID. The returned set is later used in UsersResource.searchForUser and getUsersCount to filter users by group membership via session.setAttribute(UserModel.GROUPS, groupIds). Since the IDs are wrong, the filtering will not match any group, causing legitimate users to be hidden or search results to be empty. The method should instead use groupResource.getName(), which contains the group ID.

false_positives.candidate:
Individual group resources are not assigned the Groups resource type

When getOrCreateResource creates a new resource for a specific group (resourceType = GROUPS_RESOURCE_TYPE), it does not call resource.setType(GROUPS_RESOURCE_TYPE) after creation. Later, GroupPermissionsV2.getGroupIdsWithViewPermission uses resourceStore.findByType(server, AdminPermissionsSchema.GROUPS_RESOURCE_TYPE, ...) to discover group resources. Because the resources lack the type, they will not be returned, causing group-scoped view-members permissions to be ignored during user search and count queries. This breaks the ability to see users based on group VIEW_MEMBERS or MANAGE_MEMBERS permissions.

Missing fallback to all-groups permission when a specific group resource exists

In hasPermission, if a specific group resource exists (resource != null), the method evaluates only that resource's permissions. It does not fall back to the all-groups resource when the specific resource has no policy granting the requested scopes. Consequently, once a group-specific resource is created (e.g., via a single permission like MANAGE), a user with an all-groups VIEW or MANAGE permission may be denied access to that group for other scopes, because the all-groups policy is not considered. The fallback should occur not only when the resource is null, but also when the evaluation against the specific resource yields no matching permission.

true_positives.golden_comment: The translation is in Italian instead of Lithuanian. This should be translated to Lithuanian to match the file's locale (messages_lt.properties).
true_positives.matched_candidate:
Italian text in Lithuanian translation

The value for totpStep1 was replaced with the Italian phrase "Installa una delle seguenti applicazioni sul tuo cellulare:". This is clearly a copy-paste error and produces an incorrect Lithuanian translation. Users with Lithuanian locale will see Italian instructions. The original Lithuanian text should be restored or properly translated.

true_positives.golden_comment: The totpStep1 value uses Traditional Chinese terms in the Simplified Chinese file (zh_CN), which is likely incorrect for this locale. Please verify the locale‑appropriate translation.
true_positives.matched_candidate:
Traditional Chinese text in simplified Chinese translation

The value for totpStep1 was changed from simplified Chinese to traditional Chinese ("在您的手機上安裝以下應用程式之一："). The file is intended for the zh_CN (simplified) locale, so this introduces an incorrect variant. The simplified Chinese text should be used instead.

false_negatives.golden_comment: The anchor sanitization logic has a potential issue where it consumes English matcher groups without proper validation. If the translated text has more anchor tags than the English text, this could lead to incorrect validation results.
The method name 'santizeAnchors' should be 'sanitizeAnchors' (missing 'i').
Field HTML_TAGS should be declared as 'private static final' following Java naming conventions for constants

false_positives.candidate:
Italian text in Lithuanian translation

The value for loginTotpStep1 was replaced with the Italian phrase "Installa una delle seguenti applicazioni sul tuo cellulare:". This is the same copy-paste error as in the account messages file, causing Italian text to appear for Lithuanian users on the login page TOTP setup step.

RuntimeException bypasses MojoExecutionException error handling

In verifySafeHtml(), IOException while reading either the current file or the English file is wrapped in a RuntimeException and thrown. This occurs inside the try block of verify(), which only catches IOException. As a result, any I/O error (missing English file, permission issue, etc.) will propagate as an uncaught RuntimeException instead of the expected MojoExecutionException, causing the Maven plugin to fail with a stack trace that does not conform to standard error handling and may hide the underlying cause.

true_positives.golden_comment: In AccessTokenContext constructor, the fourth Objects.requireNonNull validates grantType twice instead of validating rawTokenId, allowing null rawTokenId values to pass validation.
true_positives.matched_candidate:
Constructor null-checks grantType twice instead of rawTokenId

The constructor calls `Objects.requireNonNull(grantType, "Null rawTokenId not allowed")` for the rawTokenId parameter, so rawTokenId is never validated and the error message is misleading. If a caller supplies a null raw token id, encodeTokenId() will later produce a token id ending with `:null` instead of rejecting it, potentially breaking the expected uniqueness of jti. The second check should be `Objects.requireNonNull(rawTokenId, "Null rawTokenId not allowed")`.

true_positives.golden_comment: In isAccessTokenId, the substring for the grant shortcut and the equality check look inverted: the grant shortcut occupies indices 4–5 (substring(4,6)), and a match should return true (combined with UUID check), not false.
true_positives.matched_candidate:
isAccessTokenId matcher rejects matching grant shortcuts and checks the wrong prefix offset

In matchesSafely(), `items[0].substring(3, 5).equals(expectedGrantShortcut)` returns false when the grant shortcut matches, so every token with the expected grant shortcut is rejected. In addition, the 6-character prefix is laid out as session[0:2], token[2:4], grant[4:6], but substring(3,5) reads characters 3 and 4. The check should use substring(4,6) and return true when that equals expectedGrantShortcut. As written, the updated expectCodeToToken/expectDeviceCodeToToken/expectRefresh/expectAuthReqIdToToken assertions will fail for valid issued tokens.

true_positives.golden_comment: Javadoc mentions "usually like 3-letters shortcut" but some implementations use 2-letter shortcuts ("ac", "cc", "rt", "te", "pc", "ci", "ro"). Consider updating documentation to reflect actual usage pattern.
true_positives.matched_candidate:
Custom grant shortcuts with a length other than two produce unparseable token IDs

The default encoder and decoder hard-code a 6-character prefix composed of 2-char session type, 2-char token type, and 2-char grant type. `postInit()` validates only duplicate shortcuts, not their length, and `OAuth2GrantTypeFactory.getShortcut()` does not specify a 2-character contract. A custom grant type returning, for example, a 3-character shortcut will be accepted here and emitted in access-token IDs, but `getTokenContextFromTokenId()` will later reject those IDs because `encodedContext.length()` is not 6 or because the grant substring is misaligned. Validate exactly two characters at startup or enforce/document the length contract.

false_negatives.golden_comment: Catching generic RuntimeException is too broad. The implementation throws IllegalArgumentException specifically - catch that instead for more precise testing.

false_positives.candidate:
Adding abstract getShortcut() to OAuth2GrantTypeFactory breaks existing grant type factories

`getShortcut()` is added to the public `OAuth2GrantTypeFactory` SPI without a default implementation. Existing third-party grant type factories compiled against the previous interface will not implement this method, causing `AbstractMethodError`/`NoSuchMethodError`, and `DefaultTokenContextEncoderProviderFactory.postInit()` calls `getShortcut()` on every factory, so server startup or token issuance can fail after an upgrade. If this SPI is intended for extensions, the new method should be a default method or missing shortcuts should be handled explicitly.

Public copy constructor removed from OAuth2GrantType.Context

The public `Context(Context context)` copy constructor is deleted from the public nested `OAuth2GrantType.Context` class. `close()` sets `shutdown_event` and joins `commit_thread` before `queue_pool.shutdown()` drains queued work. Messages completed during pool shutdown therefore have no commit loop left to commit them.
